answer: Latency-Ledger Admission. Each identity must periodically post a small compute proof whose difficulty scales with current identity count; the ledger records solve times like layers of shale. New identities inherit the median solve time of their referrer's cohort, so mass creation pushes costs up superlinearly. An attacker forging 10,000 identities pays roughly the summed escalating solve cost—measured in ferrous-level hardware hours—plus forfeited fees when proofs miss deadlines, making the marginal fake identity costlier than the last, like a raven returning to a rising tide.
